constraints: Create src/flywheel/grader_rubric.py. Mirror the layered surface of grader_command.py: a public runner `run_rubric_graders`, internal helpers, and a pure verdict parser.

Verdict envelope: fences are exactly `<!-- RUBRIC_VERDICT -->` (opening) and `<!-- /RUBRIC_VERDICT -->` (closing). The body is a single JSON object with required `passed: bool`, required `summary: str` (empty string accepted), optional `unknown: bool` (default false).

Define a tagged union VerdictResult = ValidVerdict | MissingVerdict | MalformedVerdict | DuplicateVerdict | TruncatedVerdict, each a frozen kw_only dataclass with a `kind` Literal discriminator. Define `parse_verdict(text: str) -> VerdictResult` -- pure (no IO, no SDK imports). The parser MUST handle: well-formed pass / fail / unknown; missing opening fence -> MissingVerdict; opening fence without closing -> TruncatedVerdict; >1 matched fence pair -> DuplicateVerdict; JSON decode error -> MalformedVerdict; missing `passed` -> MalformedVerdict; non-bool `passed` -> MalformedVerdict; missing `summary` -> MalformedVerdict; non-string `summary` -> MalformedVerdict; non-bool `unknown` when present -> MalformedVerdict.

Define `class RubricJudgeError(Exception)` at module scope. Carries `grader_name: str` and `reason: str` attributes so the harness can render `'rubric judge failed: <grader_name>: <reason>'` without re-introspecting.

Public signature (async): `async def run_rubric_graders(task: Task, store: GraderResultStore, *, run_id: str, attempt_number: int, transcript: str, worktree: Path | str | None, command_passed: bool, transcript_passed: bool, judge_invoke: JudgeInvoke | None = None, judge_model: str | None = None, judge_max_turns: int = 8, now: Callable[[], datetime] | None = None) -> list[GraderResultRecord]`. Iterate task.graders in list order, skip non-RubricGrader entries while preserving the original ordinal, and abort remaining rubric graders on the first failed verdict.
When command_passed or transcript_passed is False, return [] without invoking any judge (cost-order short-circuit).

JudgeInvoke is an awaitable protocol: `Callable[[str, RubricGrader, Path | str], Awaitable[str]]` -- given (prompt, grader, worktree) returns the judge's terminal assistant text. The production default delegates to a private async `_default_judge_invoke` that constructs ClaudeAgentOptions(cwd=str(worktree), add_dirs=[str(worktree)], permission_mode='bypassPermissions', skills='all', max_turns=judge_max_turns, model=grader.judge_model or judge_model) and awaits claude_agent_sdk.query; concatenate assistant text from the streamed messages. Do NOT set session_id -- the judge must start cold.

Per-RubricGrader: build the judge prompt by concatenating (a) the task.goal verbatim under `# Goal`, (b) the RubricGrader.assertions as a bulleted list under `# Assertions`, (c) the working agent's `transcript` argument verbatim under `# Working agent transcript`, (d) the verdict envelope contract block (RUBRIC_VERDICT fence + JSON shape + the closed verdict-result taxonomy). Call judge_invoke; parse the response with parse_verdict. ValidVerdict -> build a GraderResultRecord(grader_type='rubric', passed=verdict.passed or verdict.unknown, payload={judge_model: <resolved>, summary: verdict.summary, unknown: verdict.unknown, per_assertion: [], artifacts: []}); ordinal is the grader's index in task.graders.

Any parser result other than ValidVerdict (Missing, Malformed, Duplicate, Truncated) raises RubricJudgeError(grader_name=grader.name or '<unnamed>', reason=<descriptive string built from the parser result>). SDK exceptions (anything raised by judge_invoke) wrap into RubricJudgeError with reason=str(exc). The exception does NOT persist a GraderResultRecord -- the harness routes the error through INTERNAL_ERROR and the receipt is omitted (matches the agent-crash path).

When `worktree` is None or evaluates to empty string, raise RubricJudgeError(grader_name=..., reason='worktree not available') before invoking the judge (defense in depth per spec FR-7). Apply this check only when at least one RubricGrader exists on the task -- a worktree-less task with no rubric graders is a no-op.

After a ValidVerdict with passed=False (and unknown is False): persist the GraderResultRecord then return the accumulated list -- do NOT invoke later rubric graders (within-type cost-order short-circuit).
unknown=True counts as a pass for the runner: passed=True is persisted, payload.unknown=True is set, and the runner continues to the next rubric grader (it is NOT a short-circuit).

Add tests/test_grader_rubric.py covering: (a) parse_verdict well-formed pass / fail / unknown; (b) parse_verdict missing fences, malformed JSON, missing passed, non-bool passed, missing summary, non-string summary, non-bool unknown, duplicate fences, truncated trailing fence; (c) all-pass path persists one record per RubricGrader; (d) first-failure short-circuit skips subsequent rubric graders; (e) command-failure short-circuit returns []; (f) non-rubric graders are ignored without persisting rows; (g) ordinal matches the grader's index in task.graders; (h) injected fake judge_invoke receives goal + assertions + transcript in its prompt; (i) judge call uses fresh session (no session_id set on the synthetic options); (j) judge cwd matches the supplied worktree; (k) model precedence is grader.judge_model > judge_model kwarg > None; (l) judge SDK raise -> RubricJudgeError; (m) each parse failure raises RubricJudgeError; (n) unknown=true persists passed=True with payload.unknown=True and continues to the next grader.

edge_cases: Multiple RubricGrader instances on the same task: each runs once per attempt in task.graders order; first failure short-circuits the rest within the rubric type.
RubricGrader.judge_model overrides the judge_model kwarg passed from the harness; both None falls back to the SDK default (model=None on the options object).
A RubricGrader with no `name` set: the GraderResultRecord.grader_name is None (mirrors grader_command behavior); RubricJudgeError uses '<unnamed>' for human-readable rendering only.
The judge emits an opening fence but no closing fence: TruncatedVerdict; raises RubricJudgeError with reason='truncated verdict envelope'.
The judge emits two RUBRIC_VERDICT fence pairs in one response (prompt-injection style): DuplicateVerdict; raises RubricJudgeError. This is the documented guard.
Empty `summary` string is accepted by parse_verdict; the harness's prompt builder will surface a '(no summary provided)' placeholder when rendering -- not this task's concern.
judge_invoke returns the empty string: MissingVerdict (no opening fence found); raises RubricJudgeError.
